description: Write operation, the bulk variant of submit_activity: one call applies one named activity of one module to many entries (the same activity for every item; nothing else runs), each item with its own input. Use instead of N sequential submit_activity calls when creating/editing many rows — one tool turn instead of N. A per-item `ai` wholly replaces the top-level default (no partial merge). Items run sequentially fail-soft on the server: one failure does not abort the rest; per-item outcomes (success, entryId, flagged, validation details) return in `results` — use `clientRef` to correlate. Max 100 items; chunk beyond that. Guardrails match submit_activity at batch level: actor='human' rejects the whole batch; actor='hybrid', activity='changeStatus', or any state override (top-level or per-item) requires `confirmed: true`.

ai.description: Default AI traceability applied to every item that does not specify its own. Same field semantics as submit_activity.ai.

approval.description: ONLY for an activity marked actor='human' (or one refused with human_actor_blocked because its humanWhen condition holds for these values), and ONLY when the user wants it done — never unasked. Instead of performing the activity, sends it to a person to approve in the Inistate app: they see your values read-only and approve (the platform then performs it as them, with exactly these values) or reject, optionally with a reason. The activity is NOT performed now: the answer says performed: false and gives a requestId; tell the user who it went to, and read the outcome with get_approval_request when they ask. Not combined with state, comment, assignees or due. Each item becomes its own request, with this summary and these recipients.

expiresIn.description: How long it stays open: "30m", "72h" or "3d"; default 72h, at most 14d

recipients.description: Usernames of who may approve (max 10); omit for the user you act for

summary.description: Why, in one or two sentences, for the approver (plain text, max 500 characters)

as.description: With dryRun: who every item acts as. Who it acts as: { "member": username } or a position { "field": "Position", "value": "Manager" }. A position is checked, not run

field.description: Or a people-module field, e.g. Position

member.description: A member's username: the run acts as them

profile.description: The people module, when more than one has the field

value.description: ...and its value, e.g. Manager: the run checks what such a person may do

confirmed.description: REQUIRED when the activity is 'changeStatus', any per-item or top-level `state` override is supplied, or the activity's actor is 'hybrid'. Set true ONLY after surfacing the planned bulk action to the user.

dryRun.description: Rehearse it: every check the submit runs, then the submit itself inside a simulation, so automations run, documents are made in memory and AutoCount codes are checked against the book. Nothing is stored or sent. Never refused for its actor, so a human step can be rehearsed too. The answer is { ok, checks, errors } with the simulation's report (changes, automations, effects, the trace). Each item is simulated on its own, at most 20 per call: simulate a sample of a larger batch.

expect.description: With dryRun: what each item's run must do. What the run must do, e.g. { "check": "automation", "automation": "Post the voucher", "equals": "Completed" }, { "check": "state", "equals": "Posted" }, { "check": "field", "module": "Cash Book", "field": "Amount", "equals": 381.9 }, { "check": "preflight" } (every AutoCount code is in the book), { "check": "allowed", "equals": false }. None: the run must go through

check.description: ok, failed, created, changed, deleted, field, lines, state, branch, automation, notification, effect, preflight or allowed

items.description: 1-100 items. Each item carries only what differs from the top-level activity.

ai.description: Optional per-item ai override. Wholly replaces top-level ai for this item.

clientRef.description: Optional caller-supplied correlation id, echoed back on the result.

comment.description: Optional. Only when necessary to communicate with the user directly. Be concise; leave the detail in the fields.

input.description: Field values keyed by display name. Same shape as submit_activity.input: Table values are arrays of row objects, numbers are JSON numbers.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID for this call. The MCP keeps no workspace between calls, so pass it every time; omit only when INISTATE_WORKSPACE_ID is configured.

title: Submit Activities (Bulk)
